title: cuscuta epithymum subsp. corsicana
intro: Cuscuta epithymum subsp. corsicana, commonly known as Dwarf Dodder, is a parasitic plant that obtains its nutrients by connecting to the vascular tissues of its host plants. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, particularly in treating menstrual disorders, and has been shown to have anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic properties. The therapeutic actions of Cuscuta epithymum subsp. corsicana include regulating menstrual cycles, relieving menstrual cramps, and reducing inflammation. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
